# Design-system components

`lib/src/ui/components/` holds the `MS`-prefixed design system. A component carries a visual contract and nothing else: an API call, a wizard or a layout signal belongs in `lib/src/ui/widgets/`.

## Folder shape

Every component is one folder, and a new one gets all four files:

```
lib/src/ui/components/<name>/
  <name>.dart          # the widget class
  <name>.recipe.dart   # WindRecipe (or recipe function) resolving className from theme tokens
  <name>.preview.dart  # preview class for the dev-only catalog
  index.dart           # barrel: the public API of this component
```

- The class is `MS<Name>`, the folder and files `snake_case`. The `MagicStarter` prefix belongs to the starter's widgets and controllers, not to a component.
- `index.dart` is exported from `lib/magic_starter.dart`; a component that barrel does not export is not part of the API.
- `index.dart` never exports the preview. A preview is registered in `starterComponentPreviews()` in `lib/previews.dart`, the dev-only barrel that keeps previews out of release builds.
- The recipe is top-level (a `WindRecipe`, or a function when a theme feeds it), so the visual contract is testable without mounting the widget; the widget takes its className from it instead of composing strings inline.
- A component never puts a `max-w-*` or a page-level `px-*` on itself: page geometry belongs to `MSPageContainer`.
- `MSButton`, `MSInput` and `MSTextarea` take `bool fullWidth = false`: a `SizedBox(width: double.infinity)` around the rendered widget rather than a width token, because Material widgets ignore cross-axis stretch (flutter/flutter#19399).

## Component contracts

- `MSCard`: `noPadding` for full-bleed list content; `CardVariant` (`surface` default, `inset`, `elevated`) drives background, border and shadow. With `noPadding` the title gets `px-6 pt-6 pb-3` so it aligns with row content, and no caller adds padding around it.
- `MSConfirmDialog.show(context, {required title, description, confirmLabel, cancelLabel, variant, onConfirm})` returns `Future<bool>`. `ConfirmDialogVariant.danger` for destructive actions (delete team, revoke session), `.warning` for caution (leave team), `.primary` for neutral. The confirm button className comes from `resolveConfirmButtonClassName(variant, modalTheme)` in `confirm_dialog.recipe.dart`, never a literal.
- `MSDataTable`: the default constructor renders every row; `MSDataTable.paginated` hands the body to magic's `MagicPaginatedListView` inside a box of `bodyHeight`, because a `ListView` needs a bound and `shrinkWrap: true` would build every row anyway. The header stays outside the scrolling body.
- `MSDataTable` listens to its paginator: reading `isEmpty` once in a build shows the empty state only when the caller already awaited the first page. Column labels and `loadingLabel` are translated strings, not keys. The column track is a wrapper rather than a `flex-1` on the cell, so `alignEnd` also applies to a flexing column.
- `MSSocialDivider`: a `WDiv` with a centred `WText(trans('auth.or_continue_with'))` between a form and the social login buttons.
- `MSSwitchRow` is a full-width `MSSwitch(label:)`. The switch lays its label out itself (a two-slot render box, not a flex row, so it works in an unbounded-width row and under `IntrinsicHeight`): the label wraps in the width beside the track, toggles the switch when tapped and is its accessibility name. A one-line label sits on the track's centre line, a wrapped one aligns to its top. A caller can override the row's className, not the label layout.
- `MSKeyValueEditor` and `MSKeyValueRow`: a controlled editor for an ordered list of key and value pairs (for example HTTP headers); every mutation emits a fresh list through `onChanged` and never mutates `value` in place.
- `MSStringValueList`: a controlled editor for a short list of distinct strings, drawn as `WBadge` chips. It commits on Enter or IME done, trims and case-insensitively de-duplicates before appending, and Backspace on an empty draft drops the last chip.
- `MSFormActions`, `MSSwitchRow`, `MSHeaderAction`, `MSKeyValueEditor` and `MSStringValueList` take every visible string as a constructor parameter, required except the optional cancel pair of `MSFormActions`: none reads a translation key of its own.
